$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §3 (coordinates), §4 (c14n/quanta), §5 (locators and typed absence), §6 (derivation), §9 (no confidence). Written from crates/engine-pdf/src/{extract,nodes}.rs. This is NOT DocumentRepresentation v0 — that envelope and the grounding projection land at M5.
title: Extract artifact (DRAFT)
description: Position-aware text runs whose origins are trustworthy, whose boxes are measured or typed-absent, and whose parse stopped rather than silently dropping content.

identity.description: artifact_type is `ethos.engine.extract.v0`; schema_version is `0.1.0`. Both DRAFT.

reading_order_rule.$comment: `single-column-v1` at v0: runs appear in content-stream order with no reordering. A two-column document therefore comes out column-by-column in whatever order the stream wrote them, which is visibly wrong and honestly so. Multi-column ships at v1 with a stable rule; pdf-inspector's flips on a single line of text (min_lines < 15), so a one-line edit reorders a whole page.

not_decoded.description: Gaps this profile declares rather than papering over.
not_decoded.$comment: Three kinds occur today. `font-widths`: a standard-14 font with no /Widths, whose built-in AFM metrics this profile does not vendor — the advance is reported absent rather than guessed. `form-xobject`: text inside a form XObject drawn with `Do` is not descended into. A predefined Adobe CMap would produce a third. Declaring them matters because an empty run list otherwise reads as 'no text here'.

index.$comment: 1-based, as the document numbers its pages.

width.$comment: Integer centipoints, AFTER rotation: a quarter turn swaps the visible dimensions.

char_codes.$comment: NOT 1:1 with `text`. A ligature is one code and several scalars: the fi glyph is code 0x03 and characters f and i. The ligature-fi fixture produces 11 characters from 9 codes.

scalar_code_mismatch.$comment: True when text.chars().count() != char_codes.len(). DECLARED, not reconciled — reconciling means dropping one side or the other. LiteParse notes the same caveat in a doc comment; this puts it on the wire where a consumer can act on it.

synthesized.description: Characters this reader inserted. Empty for a run taken verbatim from the document.
synthesized.$comment: Generalises LiteParse's `trailing_space_generated`, the best honesty field in the four surveyed projects (checklist L6). A reader that inserts a character has authored content, and unflagged authored content is indistinguishable from evidence. Flagged AT CREATION, not reconstructed later.

font_size.$comment: Integer centipoints. NEVER used as a box height — pdf-inspector's TextItem.height is literally the same variable as font_size (checklist P5), which is why a separate measured geometry exists.

mcid.$comment: Marked-content id, present only when the document supplies one via BDC. Omitted otherwise — never invented (Workbench rule 3).

pdf_locator.title: NativeLocator, PDF variant
pdf_locator.description: Required on every run. Page plus baseline origin plus advance, in integer centipoints, in the declared top-left coordinate system after page rotation.
pdf_locator.$comment: The origin is the fingerprint-critical primitive: two independent PDF stacks agree on character origin to 0.001 pt while disagreeing on height by 6.174 pt. That asymmetry is why origins are identity and boxes are inspection.

advance.$comment: OMITTED, not zero, when the document carries no width information. A standard-14 font may legally omit /Widths and expect built-in AFM metrics, which this profile does not vendor — so the advance is unknown, and unknown is what it says. The origin is unaffected: it comes from the content stream, not from the font.
